failure_summary.description: Answer carried extra echoed or descriptive words even though rules exist: 'President of Vietnam' (not 'Vietnam'), 'vitamin C' (not 'C'), 'Bull Moose Party' (not 'Bull Moose'), and 'three black teens' (a passage description) instead of the show title for a list of character names.

'A series on these' with examples gave a passage's product ('All Aboard! stamps') instead of the category noun (Trains). A noun-phrase definition clue got a niche term ('Body double') instead of the plain dictionary term (look-alike). A bare film title plus year got the star rather than the director.
Rule 4 says to keep the plural whenever the clue says 'these', which produced 'tsunamis' where the key is the bare loanword 'tsunami'.

patch.reasoning: Earlier steps that added a mandatory written Type/Evidence/Check line were all rejected, so I avoid that. The accepted step was a small, specific rule patch. This batch has two groups. First, answer-shape errors (extra category words, role phrases, descriptive phrases, a collection noun) where the correct rules sit deep in a long list or in the protected block, so I add a short top block with no required output line and one-line examples. Second, three gaps that are visible from the clue: 'these' plus examples, noun-phrase definitions, and bare film title plus year. I also soften the Rule 4 plural bullet for invariant or loanword nouns, which contradicted the key for 'tsunami'.

edits.content:
## Shape check (apply to the final answer just before the answer tags; no extra output line needed)
- STRIP ECHOES: the answer never contains a noun the clue already states, nor the clue's own 'this <noun>' label. 'this vitamin' -> 'C' (not 'vitamin C'). 'the Progressive party ... nicknamed this' -> 'Bull Moose' (not 'Bull Moose Party'). The Rule 4 head-noun exception is only for slots like 'this empire' / 'this purchase', where the bare modifier alone cannot name the thing.
- TITLE + NAME ONLY ('President Tran Duc Luong'): answer what he or she leads -> 'Vietnam', never 'President of Vietnam'.
- 'these' / 'one of these' with named examples ('A series on these of the 30s & 40s features the Daylight & the 20th Century Limited'): answer the plain CATEGORY NOUN that all the examples belong to (Trains). Do not answer with the series, stamp set, product or exhibit named in a passage title.
- LIST OF CHARACTER NAMES: answer the show/film/book TITLE found in the passage headings ('What's Happening'). Never a descriptive phrase that happens to precede the names in a passage ('three black teens').

edits.target: 'N-word' hints ('this 3-word phrase') work like a letter count: the answer must have exactly N words.
edits.content: - NOUN-PHRASE DEFINITION clues with no 'this' ('A double that visually resembles another', 'Sickle-shaped weapon of ...'): the answer is the plain common term that paraphrases the WHOLE clue, found in a dictionary or thesaurus passage (e.g. an entry glossed 'a person who is visually similar to another; a double' -> 'look-alike'). Do not pick a narrower specialist or industry term (a film-making term like 'body double') just because it contains the clue's key word. If an archive line repeats the clue but its answer is cut off, use the dictionary/thesaurus entry that glosses the clue, not the archive page's topic words.

edits.target: - Use the singular form for a generic single object ('Well', not 'wells'), but keep the plural for crops, commodities and mass categories ('Bananas') or when the clue says 'these'/'ones'.
edits.content: - Use the singular form for a generic single object ('Well', not 'wells'), but keep the plural for crops, commodities and mass categories ('Bananas') or when the clue says 'these'/'ones' (a plural category noun such as 'Trains' or 'Sails'). Exception: a foreign loanword or invariant-plural noun whose passage titles and headwords use the bare form ('Tsunami - Wikipedia', moose, sheep) is answered with that bare headword ('tsunami'), not with an added -s.

edits.target: - 'One of these <role/title>' ('the 14th one of these spiritual leaders') asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content: - A bare quoted FILM / BOOK / ALBUM title with a year and no other words ('"Rachel, Rachel"(1968)') asks for the PERSON who made it. Default to the director (or author or artist), the one passages credit as 'directed by' / 'written by', not a cast member named beside the title. Give the plain first + last name.
